title: Taiwanese Dough Animation Wins Top Prize at Japan's Educational TV Awards
summaryZh: 台灣定格動畫《我是陳派派》奪日本賞大獎。
summaryHi: ताइवान की स्टॉप-मोशन सीरीज़ "पाई पाई" ने जापान प्राइज़ का ग्रां प्री जीता।
summaryEs: La serie taiwanesa de stop-motion "Pai Pai" gana el Gran Premio del Japan Prize.
summaryJa: 台湾のストップモーション「我是陳派派」が日本賞グランプリ受賞。
summaryEn: An episode of the Taiwanese dough-figure series Pai Pai won the Grand Prix at the 53rd Japan Prize in Tokyo.
paragraphs: An episode of Pai Pai, a Taiwanese stop-motion series featuring characters made from dough, has won the Grand Prix at the Japan Prize, a long-running international contest for educational media.
The competition was established in 1965 by NHK, Japan's public broadcaster. This year's awards were presented on Thursday at With Harajuku Hall in Tokyo, alongside prizes in several other categories.

The winning 12-minute episode, Typhoon's Coming, follows ten-year-old Pai Pai as she eagerly hopes an approaching storm will force her school to close. Her friends, however, react to the news in quite different ways.

Created by TurnRhino Original Design Studio and produced with Public Television Service, the 13-part series shows its heroine tackling everyday problems with curiosity and a sense of adventure. The episode uses the children's shifting emotions to show that people respond differently to the same situation, and its light humour encourages empathy.

The contest attracted 415 entries from 59 countries and regions, the second-highest total in its history, behind the record of 423 set in 2023. A panel of 12 filmmakers and journalists judged the finalists.
A cartoon from Taiwan won a big prize in Japan this week. The prize is called the Japan Prize. It is for TV shows and videos that help people learn.
The cartoon is called Pai Pai. The people in it are made of soft dough. A team moves them a little at a time and takes many photos. This is called stop-motion.
The winning show is 12 minutes long. Its name is Typhoon's Coming. In the story, a girl called Pai Pai hopes a typhoon will close her school. But her friends feel different about the storm.
The show teaches children that people can feel different things about the same event. It is also very funny.
This year, 415 shows from 59 countries and places tried to win. Pai Pai won the top prize.
sentZh: 一部台灣卡通本週在日本贏得大獎。
這個獎叫做日本賞。
它頒給幫助人們學習的電視節目和影片。
這部卡通叫做《我是陳派派》。
裡面的人物是用軟軟的麵團做的。
團隊每次把它們移動一點點，並拍很多照片。
這叫做定格動畫。
得獎的這一集長12分鐘。
它的名字是〈颱風要來了〉。
故事裡，一個叫派派的女孩希望颱風讓學校停課。
但她的朋友對這場颱風有不同的感受。
這部節目教孩子，人們對同一件事可能有不同的感受。
它也非常好笑。
今年有來自59個國家和地區的415部作品參賽。
《我是陳派派》贏得了最高獎。

paragraphs: An episode of the Taiwanese stop-motion series Pai Pai has won the Grand Prix, the top award at this year's Japan Prize, an international competition for educational programmes.
Japan's public broadcaster NHK started the competition in 1965. The awards ceremony took place on Thursday at With Harajuku Hall in Tokyo.

The winning episode, Typhoon's Coming, is 12 minutes long. In it, a ten-year-old girl called Pai Pai hopes that a coming typhoon will close her school, but her friends have very different feelings about the storm.

Pai Pai has 13 episodes, and all the characters are made of dough. It was created by the Taiwanese studio TurnRhino Original Design and made with Public Television Service. The judges liked how the story uses humour to teach children to understand other people's feelings.
This year's competition received 415 entries from 59 countries and regions, the second-highest number ever. The record is 423 entries, set in 2023.

《我是陳派派》共13集，所有角色都是用麵團做的。
它由台灣的轉角犀牛原創設計工作室創作，並與公共電視合作製作。
評審喜歡這個故事用幽默教導孩子理解別人的感受。

paragraphs: A Taiwanese stop-motion production built around hand-shaped dough figures has claimed the Grand Prix, the highest honour at the Japan Prize, one of the world's most established competitions for educational content.

Founded by the Japanese public broadcaster NHK in 1965, the event held its latest ceremony on Thursday at With Harajuku Hall in Tokyo, where winners in a range of other categories were also recognised.

The prize-winning instalment, the 12-minute Typhoon's Coming, centres on ten-year-old Pai Pai, who is thrilled at the prospect of an approaching storm shutting her school, only to discover that her friends view the situation rather differently.

Developed by TurnRhino Original Design Studio in partnership with Public Television Service, the 13-episode series portrays a protagonist who confronts ordinary dilemmas with curiosity and an adventurous spirit. By tracing the children's fluctuating emotions, the episode illustrates how one event can provoke contrasting reactions, while its gentle humour fosters empathy.

Competition was fierce: organisers received 415 submissions from 59 countries and regions, the second-largest field on record after the 423 entries of 2023. The finalists were assessed by a jury of 12 filmmakers and journalists.
sentZh: 一部以手捏麵團人偶為主的台灣定格動畫作品，奪下日本賞最高榮譽「大獎」，日本賞是全球最具地位的教育內容比賽之一。
這項由日本公共廣播NHK在1965年創辦的活動，週四在東京With原宿Hall舉行最新一屆頒獎典禮，其他多個類別的得主也在會中受到表揚。
得獎的12分鐘單集〈颱風要來了〉以十歲的派派為主角，她對颱風可能讓學校停課感到興奮不已，卻發現朋友們對這件事的看法相當不同。
這部共13集的系列由轉角犀牛原創設計工作室與公共電視合作開發，描繪一位以好奇心和冒險精神面對日常難題的主角。
這一集藉由追蹤孩子們起伏的情緒，說明同一件事會引發截然不同的反應，而溫和的幽默則培養了同理心。
競爭十分激烈：主辦單位收到來自59個國家和地區的415件作品，是史上第二多，僅次於2023年的423件。
入圍作品由12位電影工作者和記者組成的評審團評選。

paragraphs: A Taiwanese stop-motion animation whose characters are sculpted entirely from dough has secured the Grand Prix, the most prestigious accolade at the Japan Prize, a long-established international competition dedicated to educational programming.

Inaugurated by NHK, Japan's public broadcaster, in 1965, the competition staged its most recent awards ceremony on Thursday at With Harajuku Hall in Tokyo, where accolades in numerous other categories were also conferred.

The victorious episode, a 12-minute piece entitled Typhoon's Coming, revolves around ten-year-old Pai Pai, who eagerly anticipates that an approaching typhoon will result in her school being closed. Her classmates, by contrast, perceive the impending storm from markedly different perspectives.

Conceived by TurnRhino Original Design Studio and co-produced with Public Television Service, the 13-episode series depicts a protagonist who approaches everyday predicaments with curiosity and an adventurous disposition. By charting the children's shifting emotions, the episode conveys the notion that identical circumstances can elicit divergent responses, and its understated humour cultivates empathy among young viewers.

The calibre of the competition was considerable: 415 entries were submitted from 59 countries and regions, the second-highest figure in the contest's history, surpassed only by the 423 recorded in 2023. A panel of 12 filmmakers and journalists from as many countries and regions evaluated the shortlisted works.
sentZh: 一部角色完全以麵團雕塑而成的台灣定格動畫，拿下日本賞最具聲望的「大獎」，日本賞是歷史悠久、專注於教育節目的國際比賽。
這項比賽由日本公共廣播NHK於1965年創辦，週四在東京With原宿Hall舉辦最新一屆頒獎典禮，多個其他類別的獎項也在會中頒發。
獲勝的一集是名為〈颱風要來了〉的12分鐘作品，講述十歲的派派熱切期待逼近的颱風會讓學校停課。
相比之下，她的同學們對即將來臨的颱風有著明顯不同的看法。
這部共13集的系列由轉角犀牛原創設計工作室構思、與公共電視共同製作，描繪一位以好奇心和冒險個性面對日常困境的主角。
透過記錄孩子們變化的情緒，這一集傳達出相同情境可能引發截然不同反應的觀念，而含蓄的幽默也培養了年輕觀眾的同理心。
比賽的水準相當高：共有來自59個國家和地區的415件作品參賽，是比賽史上第二多，僅次於2023年的423件。
由來自同樣多國家和地區的12位電影工作者和記者組成的評審團，評選入圍作品。
